claims.text: Role in PAD: antiplatelet monotherapy (aspirin or clopidogrel) for every patient with symptomatic lower-extremity PAD.
claims.quote: Antiplatelet monotherapy is recommended for all patients with lower extremity PAD who have symptoms (3, 4). Antiplatelet medications may modestly lessen symptoms and increase walking distance in patients with PAD; more importantly, these medications modify atherogenesis and help prevent acute coronary syndromes and transient ischemic attacks. Options for patients with symptomatic PAD include aspirin or clopidogrel orally.

claims.text: Interactions: avoid other NSAIDs (more bleeding, ↓ renal function);
claims.quote: The concurrent use of aspirin with other NSAID's should be avoided because this may increase bleeding or lead to decreased renal function.
Patients on anticoagulation therapy are at increased risk for bleeding

claims.text: Precautions: avoid in severe renal failure (GFR < 10 mL/min)
claims.quote: Avoid aspirin in patients with severe renal failure (glomerular filtration rate less than 10 mL/minute).
Avoid aspirin in patients with severe hepatic insufficiency.

claims.text: Counseling: three or more alcoholic drinks a day raises the bleeding risk.
claims.quote: Patients who consume three or more alcoholic drinks every day should be counseled about the bleeding risks involved with chronic, heavy alcohol use while taking aspirin.

claims.text: Toxicity (salicylism): early nausea, vomiting, tinnitus and hyperventilation;
claims.quote: With acute overdose, early symptoms include nausea, vomiting, tinnitus, and hyperventilation.
Salicylate poisoning causes respiratory alkalosis and, by an independent mechanism, metabolic acidosis.

claims.text: which eventually becomes the primary finding.
claims.quote: Eventually, usually as salicylate levels decrease, poorly compensated or uncompensated metabolic acidosis is the primary finding.

claims.text: Treat with activated charcoal and alkaline diuresis with extra KCl;
claims.quote: Treat with activated charcoal and alkaline diuresis with extra KCl.

claims.text: consider hemodialysis if poisoning is severe.
claims.quote: Consider hemodialysis if poisoning is severe.
